# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Harvard Pilgrim Health Care — Member Appeals
Use the appeal address printed on my denial letter
Member Services: 1-888-333-4742

**From:** Taylor Grant
Member ID: W785887548
Address: [My mailing address]
Phone: [My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-06 — Reference number POC-E71C638D4F-57015**
**Service denied:** Total hip replacement (CPT 27130)
**Governing policy:** 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review – Musculoskeletal Surgery (Hip Arthroplasty, CG 1761), https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130). The notice dated 2026-08-06 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking Harvard Pilgrim Health Care to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

I am writing this appeal myself, as the member. Below, I have set out the plan's own published criteria and shown where my medical records meet each one. The denial turned on imaging, and imaging is where my records are most specific.

---

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

The guideline states:

> "THA may be considered medically necessary as indicated in either sections 1 or 2:"

### 1. The radiographic criterion — the reason given for the denial

The guideline states:

> "Radiographic findings show evidence of advanced arthritic changes, described as Tönnis grade 2 or 3 [see Grading Appendix] or described as X-rays showing advanced changes (e.g., severe narrowing, bone-on-bone compartment collapse, subchondral sclerosis or cysts, osteophyte formation and/or bony deformity etc.)"

My imaging of 2026-05-28 was a weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph. It showed **joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes.** Those are three of the specific findings the plan's own guideline names as evidence of advanced arthritic changes: severe narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophyte formation.

The guideline also states:

> "X-rays described only as showing 'severe', 'advanced' or 'end-stage' arthritis require more definitive descriptions as stated above (weightbearing X-rays are not required)"

My report does not rely on a general word like "severe." It gives the measurement — 1 mm of remaining joint space superolaterally — and names the specific structural changes. That is the more definitive description the plan asks for, and the study was weight-bearing even though the guideline does not require that.

The guideline further states:

> "NOTE: MRI should not be the primary radiographic test used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint."

The study submitted is a plain radiograph, not an MRI, which is the test type the plan's guideline directs reviewers to rely on.

I would respectfully ask the reviewer to identify which part of this radiographic standard my 2026-05-28 X-ray was found not to meet.

### 2. Persistent pain and documented loss of function

The guideline states:

> "Persistent pain and documented loss of function with radiographic evidence of disease from any of the following:"

and

> "There is persistent pain and documented loss of function for at least 12 weeks and includes all the following"

My records document **9 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest** — well beyond the 12 weeks the plan's criterion describes. My documented loss of function includes: I walk with a cane, I am limited to about one block, and I cannot put on my shoes without help.

### 3. Physical examination findings

The guideline states:

> "Physical exam (PE) demonstrates findings of hip pathology as evidence by one or more of the following (PE is not required if bone-on-bone narrowing is present on X-ray):"

and lists, among the findings:

> "Painful, limited range of motion or antalgic gait"

My examination documents **positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.** Painful, limited range of motion is exactly one of the findings the plan lists.

### 4. Failed non-operative treatment

The guideline states:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least two of the following (1–3,5):"

and lists, among those options:

> "Protected weight-bearing with cane, walker, or crutches"

> "Physician supervised exercise program (including home exercise program)"

My records show **both** of these:

- **Supervised physical therapy** focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait — **16 weeks, from 2026-02-19 to 2026-06-11, 20 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. Sixteen weeks exceeds the 12 weeks the criterion describes.
- **Protected weight-bearing with a cane**, which I use to walk.

In addition, I took **NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief**, and I had a **corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-26 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.**

The guideline also asks the reviewer to consider:

> "Type and duration of non-operative management modalities"

The type and duration are both in the record: 16 weeks and 20 visits of supervised physical therapy, 8 months of NSAIDs, an injection, and ongoing cane use.

### 5. The injection timing rule

The guideline states:

> "No corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery (1,7–9)"

My only injection was on **2026-03-26**. More than 12 weeks have already passed since that date, and my surgery is scheduled for [scheduled surgery date — to be completed]. This criterion is satisfied.

### 6. Medical optimization

The guideline states:

> "Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery, and any treatable comorbidities are adequately medically managed such as diabetes, nicotine addiction, or an excessively high body mass index (BMI)."

My records document **no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.**

### 7. This is not an asymptomatic case

The guideline states:

> "There is no medical necessity to perform THA in individuals with severe radiological disease and no symptoms, except in the case of malignancy."

This exclusion does not describe me. I have 9 months of progressive pain, I walk with a cane, I am limited to one block, and I cannot dress my own feet. My symptoms and my imaging point the same direction.

---

## A note on the criteria I was able to review

Several of the guideline passages above end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the material available to me. I am not able to address requirements I have not seen. I am asking Harvard Pilgrim Health Care to identify, in writing, the specific criterion or criteria from the 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review – Musculoskeletal Surgery (Hip Arthroplasty, CG 1761) that my request was found not to meet, and the clinical basis for that finding. Any statement in this letter that is not inside quotation marks is my own summary of my records, not the plan's language.

---

## What I am requesting

I ask that this denial be reconsidered and that the total hip replacement (CPT 27130) requested by Dr. Duval be approved. Specifically, I request:

1. A full review by a physician reviewer, preferably one board-certified in orthopedic surgery;
2. A written explanation of which specific guideline criterion was not met, if the denial is upheld; and
3. A copy of the complete clinical criteria applied to my case.

I am also happy to have Dr. Duval provide any additional records or clarification the reviewer needs. Please let me know what would be helpful.

I understand that my appeal must be received by **2027-02-02**, which is 180 days from the date of the notice. I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I can be reached through Member Services at **1-888-333-4742** if anything further is needed.

Thank you for taking the time to look at this again.

Sincerely,

**Taylor Grant**
Member ID: W785887548
Reference number: POC-E71C638D4F-57015
Date of birth: [My date of birth]
Signature: ______________________
Date: ______________________

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-06
- Radiology report, weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph, 2026-05-28
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-02-19 to 2026-06-11, 20 visits)
- Office notes from Dr. Duval, orthopedic surgery
- [Any other records I am enclosing]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
